program.packer_note: no LZEXE/PKLITE signature: a 32-byte header, ZERO relocations, entry 0991:000E. The stub copies itself to the top of its own block and far-returns there, then decompresses the game to the load segment.
program.note: the game proper. INTRO.EXE is the separate 320x200 intro sequence (assets/PIC is its 64000-byte mode-13h picture) and is not what plays.

boot.comment: No boot image is needed: the stub is fast and the game is playable straight from the EXE (scripts/play.py). Recorded here so a boot image can be cut later without re-deriving it.
boot.canonical_entry_comment: The unpack stub reaches the game's own first instruction after 574160 guest instructions, with SS:SP = 22B3:1C00. CS == 1010h IS the load segment, so 'CS == 1010h' alone identifies game code for the whole session.

config_file.comment: 28 bytes of KEY BINDINGS, read once at startup through INT 21h AH=3Dh/3Fh — pairs of (break, make) scancodes followed by the player/option bytes. The shipped file is: up 48h, down 50h, left 4Bh, right 4Dh, space 39h, left-ctrl 1Dh, I 17h, K 25h, J 24h, L 26h, A 1Eh, then 00 01 02 03 00 00. It is DATA, not a launch detail — the game re-reads nothing and writes it only from its own SETUP screen.

pacing.comment: Measured, not chosen. The game NEVER programs PIT channel 0 (only channel 2, for the speaker), so it runs on the BIOS 18.2065 Hz tick, and it hooks INT 1Ch — the BIOS user tick hook — not INT 08h.
pacing.frame_heads_comment: THE tick seam. 1010:163C is 'has a tick arrived?' (cmp byte [1975:204F],0 / jne) and 1643 is the spin it falls into when one has not; 164A consumes the flag. The timer ISR at 1010:1355 sets [204F] = FFh as its first act, so one pass of this gate IS one displayed frame — and with no timer IRQs the game parks here exclusively.
pacing.timer_irqs_comment: The flag is a BOOLEAN, not a counter: ticks delivered in a lump collapse into one frame and the game silently runs slow. One per boundary is the only rate that matches the hardware.
pacing.simulation_hz_comment: The game's own definition of a second, not a rounding: its ISR keeps a counter at [204C], compares it against 12h and only then steps the level clock (1010:1374..137F) — 18 ticks per second, which is what the 'time left' display in the HUD counts down with. 1 * 18 = 18 Hz against the hardware's 18.2065 Hz, 1.1% slow.
pacing.step_budget_comment: Generous because a level load decompresses a whole IFF ILBM (GFX/NN.IMG) with no pass through the tick gate; the budget only decides how many guest-fallback frames that load is cut into.

presentation.comment: A TWEAKED VGA mode with no BIOS number. The game sets BIOS mode 12h (640x480x16 planar) and then rewrites the CRTC and turns on the attribute controller's 8-bit-colour bit, which makes the four planes hold ONE BYTE per pixel indexing the DAC directly — the unchained 256-colour 'Mode X' family. Everything below is read back out of the hardware by port_forge; none of it is declared.
presentation.aspect_ratio_comment: SQUARE PIXELS (256:232 = 32:29), derived rather than assumed. The mode is 512 active dots of a 25.175 MHz clock (half-rate in 256-colour, so 256 pixels) over 464 active scan lines of a 524-line frame (Maximum Scan Line 1, so 232 rows). Against VGA's square-pixel reference — 640 dots at the same clock filling the screen width, 480 of 525 lines filling its height — that is 0.800 x 0.967 of a 4:3 screen = 1.103:1, and 256/232 = 1.103. It checks out in the artwork too: the playfield is 15x11 tiles of 16x16 pixels.

raster_geometry.comment: For reference when reading a screenshot against the registers. CRTC after the tweak: 5F 3F 50 82 4C 80 0B 3E 00 41 .. E2 0C CF 20 00 E7 04 C3, attribute mode control 41h.
raster_geometry.raster: 512x464 (Horizontal Display End 64 char clocks x 8 dots; Vertical Display End 463 + 1)
raster_geometry.row_stride_comment: CRTC Offset 20h x 2 = 64 bytes per plane per row, i.e. 256 pixels across four planes — the visible width exactly, no scroll margin.
raster_geometry.double_buffered_comment: The game writes only CRTC 0Ch (start address high) and flips between 2540h and 9F40h once per tick; 0Dh stays 40h. Both pages hold a full screen.

input.mouse_comment: Dyna Blaster never calls INT 33h. It is played on the keyboard (bindings in DYNA.CFG) and offers a joystick it probes through INT 15h AH=84h, which reports none present.
input.keys_comment: Defaults from the shipped DYNA.CFG: arrows move, SPACE drops a bomb, LEFT CTRL detonates. Player 2 is I/K/J/L with A.

audio.comment: Measured over 200 Minstr of attract-mode play with a Sound Blaster attached: 3228 writes to port 42h and 420 to port 61h — the PC speaker is doing the music and the effects.

sound_blaster.comment: The game sweeps the six standard SB bases 210h, 220h, 230h, 240h, 250h, 260h. At each it resets the DSP at base+6 and runs an OPL detection at base+8/base+9 — it never looks at the AdLib port 388h. With a card at 220h it finds both the DSP and the FM chip, then probes the IRQ by unmasking IRQ0 alone and timing PIT channel 0 (which it leaves at reload FFFFh, 18.2068 Hz — the BIOS rate for all practical purposes).

data_files.comment: What the game reads, for reference. Paths arrive with DOS backslashes and in lower case ('gfx\19.img').
data_files.GFX/NN.IMG: IFF ILBM, 320x200, 8 bitplanes (256 colours), ByteRun1 compressed, 5:6 pixel aspect — the Amiga heritage showing. The game scans the loaded file for the 'BODY' chunk itself and unpacks from there.
data_files.DYNA.COD: the plain-text level password table ('LEVEL 1.1  MBHLJQHY' ...).
data_files.PIC: 64000 bytes = one 320x200 mode-13h screen, used by INTRO.EXE.
